title: Forward Notice: Tokenisation and Digital Payment Regulation
scope: Regulation that creates deadlines or obligations for blockchain infrastructure vendors: oracle networks, cross-chain interoperability, proof-of-reserve and NAV reporting, tokenised fund workflow.

definitions.direct: May regulate the vendor's own activity or designation.
definitions.passed down via customers: A regulated customer must demand controls or contract terms from its vendors.
definitions.demand driver: Creates a use case without imposing a vendor obligation.
definitions.constraint: Limits how a vendor can design, price or operate, or leaves the perimeter unsettled.

items.instrument: GENIUS Act (payment stablecoins)

key_dates.note: Enacted
Earlier of this date (18 months after enactment) or 120 days after final implementing rules
Section 3: digital asset service providers may not offer or sell a payment stablecoin in the US unless issued by a permitted issuer

items.who_is_obliged: Payment stablecoin issuers; digital asset service providers offering or selling stablecoins
items.vendor_effect_note: Issuers carry the reserve, monthly disclosure and examination duties; infrastructure vendors meet them through issuer contracts unless they themselves offer or sell stablecoins.

items.instrument: OCC proposed rule implementing GENIUS Act for OCC-supervised issuers

key_dates.note: Proposal published (OCC Bulletin 2026-3); comment close not independently confirmed

items.who_is_obliged: OCC-supervised payment stablecoin issuers and applicants
items.vendor_effect_note: Reserve, custody and control requirements on issuers are likely to flow into vendor contracts once final.

items.instrument: FDIC proposed rule implementing GENIUS Act for FDIC-supervised issuers

key_dates.note: Published in the Federal Register; comments due 60 days after publication, calendar date not independently confirmed

items.who_is_obliged: FDIC-supervised payment stablecoin issuers and insured depository institutions
items.vendor_effect_note: Issuer-level requirements; vendors affected through due diligence and contract terms.

items.instrument: Federal Reserve proposed rule implementing GENIUS Act for Board-supervised issuers

key_dates.note: Comments must be received by 30 November 2026

items.who_is_obliged: Board-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers and custodians
items.vendor_effect_note: Covers reserves, custodians, rehypothecation and yield arrangements with third parties; a reported reference to smart-contract and blockchain-monitoring providers could not be confirmed in the published text.

items.instrument: Treasury proposed rule on GENIUS Act section 3 (offering and issuance restrictions)

key_dates.note: Comments on or before 19 October 2026
Statutory restriction on digital asset service providers offering unpermitted stablecoins

items.who_is_obliged: Issuers and digital asset service providers that offer or sell payment stablecoins
items.vendor_effect_note: Can apply directly to a vendor that itself offers or sells stablecoins to US persons; otherwise not.

items.instrument: Treasury report to Congress on technologies to counter illicit finance in digital assets

key_dates.note: Report published March 2026; not a binding rule

items.vendor_effect_note: Discusses tracing across bridges and tracking smart contracts, signalling demand for transfer data and monitoring rather than imposing duties.

items.instrument: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633)

key_dates.note: Introduced; no enacted application date

items.vendor_effect_note: Market-structure perimeter for digital commodities, blockchain systems and DeFi still unsettled; no enacted oracle or interoperability licence.

items.instrument: SEC interpretation of securities laws for certain cryptoassets, joined by the CFTC

key_dates.note: Interpretation issued with token taxonomy

items.who_is_obliged: Persons undertaking securities or commodities activities
items.vendor_effect_note: Sets a token taxonomy (including digital commodities and when an investment contract attaches); it does not classify every token as a commodity or name individual tokens in the release.

items.instrument: SEC innovation exemption for tokenized-stock venues

key_dates.note: Temporary, conditional exemptive relief; permanent rulemaking date not confirmed

items.who_is_obliged: Qualifying venues and covered liquidity providers
items.vendor_effect_note: Opens a defined set of tokenized-stock venues that need pricing, settlement and corporate-action data.

items.instrument: CFTC proposed rule including certain event contracts in the definition of swap

key_dates.note: Proposed; comments due 30 days after Federal Register publication, calendar date not yet set

items.who_is_obliged: Event-contract venues and intermediaries, if adopted
items.vendor_effect_note: Would bring sports, political, cultural and weather event contracts into swap regulation, raising the bar for resolution data integrity.

items.instrument: CFTC approval of KalshiEX BTCPERP and policy on listing perpetual contracts

key_dates.note: BTCPERP approved
Policy statement on perpetual contract listings

items.vendor_effect_note: Case-by-case approval of perpetuals increases demand for reliable spot reference prices; approval does not extend to any feed or on-chain venue.

items.instrument: OFAC sanctions guidance specific to bridges or smart-contract infrastructure
items.vendor_effect_note: No bridge- or oracle-specific OFAC rule since 2025 could be confirmed; general sanctions screening applies wherever a vendor performs a controlled service.

items.instrument: MiCA CASP transitional period (Article 143) and MiCA review

key_dates.note: Latest end of CASP grandfathering; member states could shorten it
MiCA review targeted consultation, including questions on DeFi protocol and smart-contract certification

items.who_is_obliged: Cryptoasset service providers; potentially DeFi actors in future
items.vendor_effect_note: Customers must now hold national CASP authorisation; DeFi certification is a question in consultation, not an adopted rule.

items.instrument: DORA Articles 28 to 30 (ICT third-party contract terms)

key_dates.note: DORA applies

items.vendor_effect_note: Banks and other financial entities must write service levels, security, incident support, audit and exit terms into contracts with ICT vendors, whether or not the vendor is designated.

items.instrument: DORA critical ICT third-party provider designations

key_dates.note: First designations published; next round not confirmed

items.vendor_effect_note: Direct oversight applies only to named designees; no blockchain oracle or interoperability provider has been confirmed on the list.

items.instrument: Revised Benchmarks Regulation (EU) 2025/914

key_dates.note: Revised, narrower scope applies

items.who_is_obliged: Administrators of critical and significant benchmarks, specified climate and commodity benchmarks
items.vendor_effect_note: An on-chain reference used to determine payments or values of financial instruments needs a product-level perimeter test; the significant-benchmark threshold is EUR 50 billion.

items.instrument: Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (travel rule)

key_dates.note: Applies

items.vendor_effect_note: Originator and beneficiary data must travel with covered transfers, including from self-hosted addresses; messaging vendors may receive data specifications from CASPs.

items.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 and AMLA

key_dates.note: AMLR general application; AMLA self-hosted address guidelines indicated
AMLA planned start of direct supervision of selected entities (year only)

items.vendor_effect_note: No anonymous cryptoasset accounts and risk mitigation for self-hosted addresses; vendors see screening and data specifications from obliged customers.

items.instrument: Digital euro legislative proposal

key_dates.note: Parliament mandate to begin negotiations; application date not set

items.vendor_effect_note: Future retail CBDC creates interoperability questions but no current vendor obligation.

items.instrument: DLT Pilot Regime and ECB Pontes wholesale DLT settlement

key_dates.note: DLT Pilot applies
Pontes launch reported by ECB

items.who_is_obliged: Authorised DLT market infrastructures and participants
items.vendor_effect_note: Central bank money settlement for DLT transactions creates integration demand between ledgers; no mandatory vendor certification.

items.instrument: New cryptoasset regulated activities and FCA perimeter guidance (PS26/18)

key_dates.note: New FSMA cryptoasset regulated activities commence

items.who_is_obliged: Firms performing specified UK cryptoasset activities
items.vendor_effect_note: Infrastructure, APIs and data feeds are not automatically regulated; authorisation turns on performing an in-scope activity such as custody or operating a trading platform.

items.instrument: FCA stablecoin issuance rules (PS26/10)

key_dates.note: Applies with the new regulated activities regime

items.vendor_effect_note: Independent reasonable-assurance review of backing, disclosure and outsourcing controls create demand for assurance-ready reserve data.

items.instrument: Bank of England systemic sterling stablecoin policy and draft Code

key_dates.note: Code consultation closed
Intended finalisation by end-2026; not an application date

items.who_is_obliged: Systemic sterling stablecoin issuers recognised by HM Treasury
items.vendor_effect_note: Systemic issuer standards will shape what issuers require of reserve, reporting and settlement providers.

items.instrument: Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777)
items.body: HM Treasury / Bank of England / PRA / FCA

key_dates.note: Four designations take effect

items.who_is_obliged: Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL, Google Cloud EMEA Limited, Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited, Oracle Corporation UK Limited
items.vendor_effect_note: Applies only to the four named cloud providers; Oracle Corporation UK Limited is a database company, not a blockchain oracle. No blockchain provider designated.

items.instrument: UK Benchmarks Regulation reform consultation

key_dates.note: FCA statement welcoming consultation; close and commencement not confirmed

items.vendor_effect_note: A reformed UK perimeter could change whether data used to settle financial contracts is administered as a benchmark.

items.instrument: Digital Securities Sandbox and Synchronisation Lab

key_dates.note: Sandbox participants may apply to use certain stablecoins as settlement assets

items.vendor_effect_note: Live testing of synchronised ledger and central bank money settlement (the Synchronisation Lab runs about six months from spring 2026, end date not confirmed) creates integration demand from participants.

items.instrument: Digital Token Service Provider regime

key_dates.note: Applies

items.who_is_obliged: Singapore-based providers serving customers solely outside Singapore, for in-scope services
items.vendor_effect_note: Applies only if a vendor provides a regulated digital token service; utility or governance token services are outside scope.

items.instrument: Stablecoin framework legislation consultation and Project Guardian
items.vendor_effect_note: Guardian sets industry practice for tokenized funds and interoperability; stablecoin legislation timing not confirmed.

items.instrument: Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) issuer licensing

key_dates.note: Licence effective date shown on public register for a licensed issuer; not a general deadline

items.vendor_effect_note: Licensed issuers carry reserve and redemption duties that pass to their infrastructure suppliers.

items.instrument: SFC tokenisation circular and HKMA Project Ensemble

key_dates.note: Ensemble next phase for real-value tokenised deposit transactions

items.vendor_effect_note: Product providers stay responsible for tokenised product arrangements; Ensemble drives tokenised deposit interoperability.

items.instrument: CBUAE Payment Token Services Regulation and VARA Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook
items.who_is_obliged: Payment token service providers and in-scope issuers
items.vendor_effect_note: Direct only for a vendor performing a covered payment-token or issuance service.

items.instrument: ADGM FSRA virtual asset staking framework

key_dates.note: Framework finalised

items.vendor_effect_note: Duties fall on authorised intermediaries, not on staking or node infrastructure generally.

items.instrument: FINMA Guidance 01/2026 on custody of crypto-based assets

key_dates.note: Published

items.vendor_effect_note: Supervised firms stay responsible when using external or foreign custodians, so subcontractor controls flow to vendors.

items.instrument: Basel prudential treatment of cryptoasset exposures (SCO60)

key_dates.note: Framework version effective; national implementation varies

items.vendor_effect_note: Supervisors can add capital for weak technological infrastructure (add-on currently zero), so banks need evidence on settlement finality and reference-price controls.

items.instrument: FATF targeted report on decentralised finance

key_dates.note: Published July 2026 (month only)

items.who_is_obliged: National authorities; persons with control or sufficient influence over DeFi arrangements under local law
items.vendor_effect_note: Control tests look at upgrade and governance powers, and the report names chain-hopping and bridges as illicit-finance techniques; not a licence in itself.

items.instrument: FSB peer review, IOSCO tokenisation report and CPMI-IOSCO stablecoin guidance

key_dates.note: FSB thematic peer review (month only)
IOSCO Tokenization of Financial Assets

items.vendor_effect_note: Signals supervisory scrutiny of governance and dependencies in tokenisation; no binding cross-chain provider rule.
